authors: Daniel Jarrett, Bogdan Cebere, Tennison Liu, Alicia Curth, Mihaela van der Schaar
title: HyperImpute: Generalized Iterative Imputation with Automatic Model Selection
validity_discussion: Discusses how conditionally-specified models may not always induce valid joint distributions, and how increasing univariate model capacity embeds the true joint distribution within the parameter space of the conditionals under MAR. Quote: 'conditionally-specified models may not always induce valid joint distributions... poorly-fitting conditional models may lead to biased results... Augmenting the capacity of univariate models makes it more likely Hcom ⊂ ΠD_d=1 Hd so that the true joint distribution is embedded in the parameter space of the conditionals...'

authors: Breeshey Roskams-Hieter, Jude Wells, Sara Wade
title: Leveraging Variational Autoencoders for Multiple Data Imputation
validity_discussion: Shows that standard single imputation VAEs produce overconfident predictions and underestimate uncertainty at extreme missing values, whereas beta-VAEs combined with Rubin's multiple imputation restore empirical coverage (95% CIs) and reduce false discovery rates. Quote: 'Standard VAE (β=1) underestimates the uncertainty in multiple imputation... We find that VAEs provide poor empirical coverage of missing data, with underestimation and overconfident imputations... multiple imputation with β-VAEs yields fewer false positives and more acceptable false discovery rates.'

authors: Innocent G. Asiimwe, Tao You, Daniel F. Carr, Munir Pirmohamed, Geraint Davies, Andrea L. Jorgensen
title: Improving Genotype Imputation in High-Dimensional Pharmacogenomics Using Multiple Imputation: Evaluation with Machine Learning Approaches
validity_discussion: Evaluates statistical validity by demonstrating that traditional single genotype imputation produces near-zero confidence interval coverage and false-positive associations, whereas multiple imputation pooled via Rubin's rules restores nominal 95% CI coverage (~90-94%) and reduces spurious GWAS signals. Quote: 'In simulations, only multiple imputation achieved adequate coverage (percentage of 95% confidence intervals containing the true value) exceeding a 90% nominal threshold... single-imputation methods... consistently underperformed... with near-zero coverage across all scenarios.'

authors: Ana S. Fernandes, Ian H. Jarman, Terence A. Etchells, José M. Fonseca, Elia Biganzoli, Chris Bajdik, Paulo J.G. Lisboa
title: Missing data imputation in longitudinal cohort studies - application of PLANN-ARD in breast cancer survival
validity_discussion: Addresses missing data as a nuisance during survival model training and external cohort validation, noting that listwise deletion introduces bias and reduces statistical power under MAR. Quote: 'We do not assume that missing data was a random sample in both data sets i.e. missing completely at random (MCAR) – but rather that they are missing at random (MAR)... cases with missing values can be removed... [which] may induce bias in the modelling, as well as potentially significantly reducing the statistical power of the analysis.'

authors: Carlos Traynor, Tarjinder Sahota, Helen Tomkinson, Ignacio Gonzalez-Garcia, Neil Evans, Michael Chappell
title: Imputing Biomarker Status from RWE Datasets—A Comparative Study
validity_discussion: Emphasizes that single point imputations fail to represent missing value uncertainty, requiring multiple imputation to sample from the joint PDF, preserve parameter estimate moments, minimize bias, and maintain nominal confidence interval coverage under MAR. Quote: 'The general idea of MI is to generate multiple complete datasets, analyse each dataset separately, and summarise the results... Therefore, the MI approach embraces the uncertainty in the missing values that single imputation with a point estimate cannot represent... our interest is in the distributional characteristics of the multiply imputed datasets, such as preserving parameter estimates’ moments having low bias, high coverage of confidence intervals...'
